findings.description: In section 3, EN-11 calculates the elastic modulus E by dividing the ultimate stress (506.67 MPa) by the strain recorded at the same instant (2.410 x 10^-3). This is a fundamental physics error. The elastic modulus is the slope of the linear elastic region. The ultimate stress occurs far beyond the yield point (nominal yield is 275 MPa), in the plastic deformation region.
findings.proposed_fix:
<<<< SEARCH EN-11. Taking that stress with the strain reading of 2.410 x 10^-3 recorded at the same instant, with a standard measurement uncertainty of 1.5 x 10^-5, the derived modulus E = sigma / epsilon = 210.24 GPa with a combined standard uncertainty of 2.04 GPa, that is 0.969 per cent relative. The result lies within plus or minus 3 per cent of the nominal 210 GPa used in section 2, which is the acceptance band this reference applies, and so no adjustment to the deflection calculations is warranted.
====
EN-11. The elastic modulus E cannot be derived by dividing the ultimate stress by the strain recorded at the same instant, because the ultimate stress lies in the plastic deformation region far beyond the yield point. The reported ratio of 210.24 GPa is a secant modulus, not the elastic modulus. A valid determination of E requires extracting the slope from the linear elastic portion of the coupon test data; until this is done, the validation of the 210 GPa nominal value remains incomplete.

findings.description: In section 8, EN-42 performs a least-squares regression of log10 N on linear stress amplitude (S) to derive a fatigue curve.
